concepts.title: Linear Graphs and Their Uses
concepts.definition: A linear graph plots two quantities whose graph is a straight line: plotting points from a table of values and joining them shows whether the relation between the quantities is linear, as in cost per unit or fixed charges plus rate.
concepts.key_idea: Table to points to a straight line: linearity is visible at a glance.
concepts.textbook_ref: hemh113.txt sections 13.1-13.2 (line graphs, linear graphs, some applications)
question_patterns: draw the graph of the given data and state whether it is linear
plot the points from the table and join them
does the given graph show a linear relation - justify
from the graph read the value for the given input
draw a graph for the principal and simple interest data
check which of the given tables give a linear graph

solution_steps.explain: Choose the x-axis and y-axis quantities and their scales.
Each row of the table becomes one point.
A single straight line through all points signals a linear relation.

concepts.title: Coordinates and Locating Points
concepts.definition: Every point on the plane is pinned by two coordinates - the x-coordinate measuring along the horizontal axis and the y-coordinate along the vertical - so (3, 4) sits three units right and four units up from the origin.
concepts.key_idea: Order matters: the pair (x, y) walks right first, then up.
concepts.textbook_ref: hemh113.txt sections on coordinates and the y-axis (line graphs setup)
question_patterns: write the coordinates of the given points marked on the graph
locate the point (3, 4) on the coordinate plane
what does the first number in a coordinate pair tell
in which quadrant does the given point lie
plot the given ordered pairs and join them
which point lies on the y-axis - justify

solution_steps.explain: Move along the horizontal axis by the first number.
Move parallel to the vertical axis by the second number.
The meeting place of the two guides is the point.

concepts.title: Distance-Time Graphs
concepts.definition: A distance-time graph plots journey data with distance on the vertical axis and time on the horizontal; a straight rising line shows uniform speed whose value is the distance covered divided by the time taken, a horizontal stretch shows rest, and steeper lines mean faster motion.
concepts.key_idea: The slope tells the story: steeper line, greater speed; flat line, at rest.
question_patterns: draw a distance-time graph for the given journey data
find the speed of the object from its distance-time graph
when was the object at rest according to the graph
which of the two lines shows a faster speed
read the distance covered at the given time from the graph
is the motion uniform - explain from the graph

solution_steps.explain: Uniform speed is the distance covered per unit time.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A car covers {distance} km in {time} hours moving uniformly. Find its speed.

solution_template.explain: Uniform speed equals distance over time.

worked_examples.question_pattern: From the distance-time graph, the object covers {distance} metres in {time} seconds. Calculate the speed in metres per second.

extracted_variables.distance: distance read from the graph in metres
extracted_variables.time: time read from the graph in seconds

solution_template.explain: The slope of the line is the speed.
